questions.stem: The 'Panchatantra' — one of the world's oldest collections of animal fables, attributed to the scholar Vishnu Sharma — was originally composed in which language?

options.option_text: Pali — the liturgical language of early Buddhist canonical texts
Sanskrit — the classical language of ancient Brahminic scholarship
Prakrit — a middle Indo-Aryan vernacular literary language
Apabhramsha — the transitional language of medieval north India

questions.explanation: The Panchatantra was composed in Sanskrit (c.3rd century BCE–3rd century CE) and its Arabic translation 'Kalila wa Dimna' (8th century CE) confirms the Sanskrit origin. Pali is the strongest distractor because Buddhist Jataka tales — also animal fables — are written in Pali, causing genuine confusion among test-takers.

questions.stem: R.K. Narayan's fictional South Indian town 'Malgudi' — the setting of 'Swami and Friends', 'The Guide', and 'The Man-Eater of Malgudi' — is widely accepted to be modelled after which real city?

options.option_text: Madurai, Tamil Nadu — the ancient city of the Meenakshi Amman temple
Udupi, Karnataka — celebrated for its Brahmin cuisine and ancient temples
Mysore, Karnataka — the city that shaped Narayan's entire literary imagination
Coimbatore, Tamil Nadu — the industrial city known as the Manchester of South

questions.explanation: R.K. Narayan grew up in Mysore, whose topography, climate, and social texture he transformed into Malgudi. He acknowledged this connection explicitly. Madurai is a common distractor since Narayan was Tamil-speaking and it is a prominent South Indian city — but the correct referent is Mysore in Karnataka.

questions.stem: Amrita Pritam's Punjabi novel 'Pinjar' (1950) — later adapted into a 2003 Hindi film starring Urmila Matondkar — is set against the backdrop of which historical upheaval?

options.option_text: The Partition of India and Pakistan and the communal violence of 1947
The Bengal famine of 1943 and the forced displacement of rural communities
The Jallianwala Bagh massacre and the Punjabi protest movement of 1919
The Sepoy Mutiny of 1857 and displacement of Punjabi regimental families

questions.explanation: 'Pinjar' (meaning 'The Skeleton') depicts the abduction of a Hindu woman Pooro by a Muslim man during the 1947 Partition, exploring trauma across communal lines. Amrita Pritam herself witnessed the Partition. Jallianwala Bagh is the most tempting distractor because that 1919 massacre also scarred Punjabi collective memory and is associated with Pritam's other political verse.

questions.stem: The epic Hindi poem 'Urvashi' (1961) — which reimagines the celestial apsara Urvashi's love for mortal King Pururavas and earned its author the Jnanpith Award in 1972 — was composed by which poet?

options.option_text: Sumitranandan Pant — pioneering voice of the Chhayavad Romantic movement
Harivansh Rai Bachchan — celebrated author of the famous Madhushala cycle
Ramdhari Singh Dinkar — master of virasa (heroic) Hindi verse and epics
Mahadevi Varma — called the 'Meera of modern Hindi' for her mystic verse

questions.explanation: Ramdhari Singh Dinkar wrote 'Urvashi' and won the Jnanpith Award in 1972 for it. Sumitranandan Pant (Jnanpith 1968) and Mahadevi Varma (Jnanpith 1982) are both Jnanpith winners themselves, making them strong distractors. Harivansh Rai Bachchan is the most familiar name to general test-takers, making him the most tempting wrong choice despite never winning the Jnanpith.

questions.stem: Girish Karnad's landmark Kannada play 'Tughlaq' (1964) uses the erratic reign of Sultan Muhammad bin Tughlaq primarily as an allegory for which dimension of post-independence Indian political life?

options.option_text: The Emergency of 1975 — suspension of civil liberties by Indira Gandhi's government
The Green Revolution's displacement of subsistence farmers across North India
The Partition trauma and the psychological fracture it inflicted on Indian society
The collapse of Nehruvian idealism into bureaucratic and moral disillusionment

questions.explanation: 'Tughlaq' was written in 1964 — the very year Nehru died — making the Emergency of 1975 impossible as its referent. Critics and Karnad himself confirmed the play is a parable of how grand utopian visions curdle into authoritarian failure, mirroring Nehruvian ambition. The Emergency option is the most common wrong answer since the play's political tenor superficially fits that later narrative.

questions.stem: The inaugural Jnanpith Award (1965) was conferred on G. Sankara Kurup for his poetry collection 'Odakkuzhal' (meaning 'The Flute'). This award-winning collection belongs to which Indian language?

options.option_text: Malayalam — the language of the ancient Manipravalam bilingual tradition
Kannada — the language of the medieval Vachana Shaiva poetry tradition
Tamil — the classical Dravidian language of the ancient Sangam corpus
Telugu — the language of the classical Prabandha courtly poetry tradition

questions.explanation: G. Sankara Kurup was a Malayalam poet, and 'Odakkuzhal' (1950) won the very first Jnanpith Award in 1965. Kannada is the single most tempting distractor: Karnataka has produced the most Jnanpith winners (8) of any state, leading test-takers to assume the first winner was also Kannada. Tamil and Telugu are plausible because both are classical Dravidian languages with ancient literary pedigrees.

questions.stem: Which 14th-century Kashmiri mystic poetess composed ecstatic devotional verses called 'Vakhs' that are venerated by both Shaiva Hindus and Sufi Muslims — making her the only medieval saint simultaneously claimed by both traditions in Kashmir?

options.option_text: Habba Khatoon — lyric poetess of 16th-century Mughal-era Kashmir valley
Lal Ded (Lalleshwari) — Trika Shaiva mystic and mother of Kashmiri poetry
Rupa Bhavani — 17th-century Kashmiri saint known for ecstatic Shaiva verse
Arnimal — 18th-century classical Kashmiri devotional and love-lyric poetess

questions.explanation: Lal Ded (c.1320–1392) composed Vakhs — brief, aphoristic mystical verses in Kashmiri — synthesising Trika Shaivism and early Sufi thought. She is revered as 'Lal Ded' by Hindus and 'Lalla Arifa' by Muslims. Habba Khatoon is the strongest distractor: she is the other iconic Kashmiri poetess, but she lived in the 16th century at Yusuf Shah Chak's court and composed romantic lyrics, not Vakhs.
